RATIONALE:
Q1: Option A has already failed three times in a row. #8072 moved the unblock step to group 1, #8080 moved the single-file modules to group 1, and #8091 moved the unblock step back to group 0, which is now at 16m45s. With every receiving job sitting near 15 minutes, another move only shifts the overrun somewhere else. A fifth group fixes the cause instead: each group runs `NR % total == n`, so every group's slice of the sharded poll module shrinks by about a fifth, and all steps pinned by `strategy.job-index == 0..3` keep their current groups unchanged. This does not create a new required job name. The only required check is the aggregate `CI / lint`, which already needs the whole `orchestrate-poll` job (`lint` defaults to the required check in `_pr_auto_merge_required_ci_check_name` and `scripts/release_ci_gate.sh`). `orchestrate-poll (4)` is just another entry in that matrix, so `lint`'s `needs` list and `timeout-minutes: 20` stay the same. The one guardrail that changes is in `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`:
- line 236 expects the matrix to be exactly `[0, 1, 2, 3]` and becomes `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]`;
- `test_two_level_partition_holds_across_group_and_shard_counts` already checks 5 groups;
- the live-matrix check at line 188 reads its group count from `poll_group_count()`, so it follows the new size by itself.

The release gates' `validate-scripts` jobs do not use groups and are not affected. Option C, moving the unblock step into group 4 as well, is not needed at first. It can be a follow-up if group 0 is still near the threshold after the slice shrinks.
